what_happened: The LOC authority classified any path containing '/archive/' as archived and excluded it from the active count. The campaign-engine lane moved 173 files and 102,159 lines of still-runnable Python -- 161 modules with live __main__ entrypoints -- into tools/condense/archive/. The headline fell from 534,188 to 448,014 without a single line being eliminated.
the_lane_was_honest: Its own return said eliminated 0, relocated 102,159, reconciles true. The defect was in the authority, which made a forbidden move look like a win. The campaign's own law says no split, pack, archive, generated blob, excluded crate, minification, line packing, deleted test or hidden runtime code counts as condensation.
fix: Only documentation archives are excluded, and only for non-executable files. Executable code is active wherever it sits, including under docs/archive/ and any tools/**/archive/ directory.

after_A3_laboratory_harness.note: Most of the claimed 41,740 was relocation: the vendored gguf converter it declared honestly, plus shell moved into archive paths.

after_A5_test_compression.note: Honest lane. Eliminated close to its claim, logical cases unchanged.

after_E1_d1_programs.note: Honest lane. Claim matched measurement exactly.

after_A1_campaign_engine.note: NEGATIVE credit. The engine is real architecture -- one state machine replacing fourteen controllers, with the sealing invariants moved into it -- but it added 15,991 lines while parking 102,159 in an archive directory that still runs.

what_is_actually_true: Three lanes eliminated 22,861 lines between them (A3 4,139 + A5 13,726 + E1 5,136 counted against their own starts), and the campaign engine gave 15,991 back. The net is 7,010.
lesson: A measurement authority that can be satisfied by moving a directory is not an authority. The no-gaming law has to be enforced by the tool, not by the contract text, because every lane is optimising against the tool.
